chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Hi, thanks for calling in, you're through to billing support, my name's Devin. Can I grab your account number to pull things up?

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Yeah, it's 447129. I'm calling because I was charged twice for the same thing and nobody's explained why.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Okay, let me take a look. Give me just a second while this loads up. Alright, I can see your account, and you're on the standard monthly plan, is that right?

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: That's right. So I got my statement this week and there are two charges of $89 each, both dated the 14th.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: I see that too, yes. Two charges, same amount, same day, on invoice numbers ending in 031 and 032.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Right, and I only have the one subscription, I didn't sign up for anything else, so this is really confusing to me.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: I completely understand the confusion, and I'm sorry you had to deal with seeing that on your statement without any explanation first. Let me dig into why this happened before we talk about fixing it.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: I appreciate that, I just want to understand what went wrong, honestly, more than anything.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Totally fair. Okay, so looking at the log here, it looks like there was a billing system update that ran on the 13th, and for a small number of accounts it seems to have triggered the renewal charge twice.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: So this wasn't just me.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: No, it wasn't just you, unfortunately. It looks like a batch of accounts got hit by this, and yours is one of them. I want to be upfront that this is a duplicate charge caused by an error on our end, not anything you did.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Okay, that actually helps, I was starting to wonder if I'd accidentally clicked something twice during checkout last month.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: No, nothing like that, this is squarely on us. So let's get this corrected. I can process a refund for the second charge right now, the one on invoice 032.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Okay, and how long does a refund like that usually take to actually show up?

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Typically three to five business days depending on your bank, sometimes it posts faster, but I don't want to promise less than five and have you disappointed.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: That's fine, I just wanted a realistic number instead of a vague answer.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Absolutely fair. Let me go ahead and submit that now. Okay, the refund for $89 against invoice 032 has been submitted, and you should get a confirmation email within the next few minutes.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Great, thank you. Can I ask, is there anything else on my account I should check, given that this billing update apparently affected a batch of people?

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Good question, let me check your last three statements just to be thorough. Give me a moment. Okay, looking back at the last three months, everything before this looks normal, one charge per cycle, no duplicates.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Okay, good, that's reassuring. What about going forward, is this going to happen again next month?

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: It shouldn't. The team pushed a fix for the underlying issue on the 15th, and I can see your account is flagged as one that was affected, which means it'll get an extra manual check before next month's renewal runs.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Okay, that's good to hear, I don't want to be back on the phone next month having the same conversation.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Completely understandable, and honestly if it does happen again, mention this call, the reference number is r-8812, and whoever you speak to will be able to see the history immediately.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Got it, I'll write that down. r-8812

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: That's right. Now, I also want to check, did the duplicate charge cause any actual problems for you, like an overdraft or anything with your bank?

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: It didn't cause an overdraft, thankfully, but it did throw off my budgeting for the week, since I wasn't expecting to see an extra $89 gone.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: That's frustrating, and I'm sorry about that. I can also add a small credit to your account for the inconvenience, on top of the refund, if that would help.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Oh, that's not necessary, but I won't say no either.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: I'll go ahead and add a $15 account credit, that'll show up as a reduction on your next invoice.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Okay, thank you, that's a nice gesture, I wasn't expecting that honestly.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Of course. Is there anything else on the account you wanted to go over while I have everything pulled up?

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Actually yet, while I'm here, my invoice email address is still my old one, can we update that too?

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Sure, what would you like it changed to?

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: It's dana.rayaset, let's just say a personal email domain, I'll type it in on the portal actually since it's easier than saying it out loud.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: That works too, if you go to account settings, then billing preferences, there's an update email field right at the top, and it takes effect immediately, no confirmation delay.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Perfect, I'll do that after we hang up. Just to confirm one more time, the refund is definitely processing.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Yes, confirmed, refund submitted for the $89 duplicate charge, plus the $15 credit for the inconvenience, and a flag on your account for extra review before next month's renewal.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: That covers everything I was worried about. Thank you for actually explaining what happened instead of just saying you'll look into it.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Of course, that's exactly what we should be doing. I know getting a surprise charge like that is stressful, especially when the explanation isn't obvious.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: It really was stressful for about ten minutes this morning until I calmed down enough to call in.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Completely understandable reaction. Is there anything else I can help with today, or are we good to close this out?

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: I think we're good. Thanks again, Devin, this actually went a lot smoother than I expected.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Happy to help. You'll get that confirmation email shortly, and don't hesitate to call back with that reference number if anything looks off next cycle.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Will do. Have a good one.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: You too, take care.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Actually, hold on, one more thing just occurred to me. Will this duplicate charge situation affect my loyalty tier or anything like that, since it might show two renewal events instead of one?

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Good catch, let me check that. Looking at your loyalty tier calculation, it's based on total month subscribed, not number of transactions, so a duplicate charge on the same day wouldn't push you into a different tier either way.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Okay, that's a relief. I didn't want this mistake to somehow bump me into a different pricing tier by accident.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: No, that wouldn't happen, but I appreciate you asking, it's a reasonable thing to worry about given everything else that went wrong here.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: Yeah, once one thing goes sideways you start double checking everything else on the account, at least I do.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: That's a very normal reaction, honestly. While I have you, I'll also leave a note on the account summarizing today's call, the refund, the credit, and the email update request, so if anyone else looks at this account later they have full context.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: That's helpful, I like that it won't just disappear into a call log somewhere with no explanation.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Exactly, that's the goal. Alright, I think that really does cover everything now. Take care, and again, sorry for the hassle with the duplicate charge.

chunks.speaker: B
chunks.text: No worries, thanks for sorting it out quickly. Bye now.

chunks.speaker: A
chunks.text: Bye.
